newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-PREKI'S LATE GOAL LEADS KANSAS CITY TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PREKI'S LATE GOAL LEADS KANSAS CITY TO VICTORY.

text.p: Preki scored his second goal of the game with three minutes remaining in regulation to lift the Kansas City Wizards to a 3-2 Major League Soccer victory over the San Jose Clash Sunday.

Mark Chung also scored for the Wizards (8-4), who solidified their Western Conference lead with their second win within 48 hours. U.S. international striker Eric Wynalda and Lawrence Lozzano scored for the struggling Clash (4-9).

On Friday, Frank Klopas, Matt McKeon and Chung recorded shootout goals as the Wizards won the tie-breaker, 3-1, for a 2-1 win over the Dallas Burn (7-6) in Dallas, Texas. Kansas City goalkeeper Mike Ammann, who made nine saves during regulation, stopped one shootout attempt and forced two players to miss.
Mexican Damian Alvarez had given the Burn the lead in the 49th minute, but Paul Wright equalised three minutes later.

Despite playing without its three most dangerous offensive players, D.C. United (10-3) rolled to a 5-0 victory over the Colorado Rapids (5-8), the Eastern Conference leader's fifth consecutive win, in Washington, D.C.

U.S. National Team captain John Harkes scored the first goal and set up the second one, by Tony Sanneh. Clint Peay, Richie Williams and Jesse Marsch also tallied for United, who played without Bolivians Jaime Moreno and Marco Etcheverry and El Salvadoran Raul Diaz Arce, who played in World Cup qualifiers on Sunday.

The Tampa Bay Mutiny (6-6) ended a four-game losing streak, downing the Columbus Crew, 3-1, in Tampa, Florida. Alan Prampin, who created Italian Giuseppe Galderisi's opening goal, broke a 1-1 tie in the 56th minute. Marcelo Carrera scored for the Crew (6-7), who have lost five straight matches.

Former Italian World Cup goalkeeper Walter Zenga made several important saves in regulation and in the shootout to boost the New England Revolution (9-4) to a 1-0 victory over the Los Angeles Galaxy (3-9) in Foxboro, Massachusetts. Zenga stopped shots by Bryan Taylor, Harut Karapetyan and Danny Pena in regulation.
Imad Baba and Argentine Alberto Naveda scored in the tie-breaker for the Revolution, who placed only two shots on goal in regulation.
The New York/New Jersey MetroStars (5-7), who did not have a regular-season game scheduled, stunned Sampdoria of Italy, 1-0, in a friendly on a first-half goal by Colombian Antony De Avila.
